statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation or definition of the Finite Difference Jacobian, as they contain no discussion of multivariable functions, vector-valued functions, partial derivatives, or Jacobian matrices; the sources exclusively present numerical differentiation and finite difference formulas for single-variable scalar functions f(x).

symbols.meaning: real-valued function being evaluated or differentiated
point at which the derivative is estimated
step size between discrete sample points
continuous derivative operator mapping f to f'

properties.property: Numerical differentiation algorithms estimate the derivative of a mathematical function using values of the function at a set of discrete points rather than providing exact analytical expressions.
properties.why: enables derivative approximation from discrete data or simulation points where analytical expressions are unavailable

properties.property: Classical finite-difference approximations for numerical differentiation are ill-conditioned.
properties.why: evaluations suffer from subtractive cancellation and numerical instability when step sizes are small

properties.property: The difference operator \Delta_h is linear and satisfies a discrete Leibniz product rule: \Delta_h(fg)(x) = (\Delta_h f(x))g(x+h) + f(x)(\Delta_h g(x)).
properties.why: follows from the definition of the shift operator T_h and the difference operator \Delta_h = T_h - I

properties.property: The continuous derivative operator D can be formally expressed via the difference operator as h D = \ln(1 + \Delta_h) = \Delta_h - \frac{1}{2}\Delta_h^2 + \frac{1}{3}\Delta_h^3 - \cdots.
properties.why: obtained by formally applying Taylor series to yield \Delta_h = e^{h D} - I and inverting the exponential

assumptions.assumption: Function values can be evaluated at discrete offsets x + kh near x
assumptions.breaks_when: The function is undefined, inaccessible, or non-evaluable at discrete sampled points

assumptions.assumption: The function f is sufficiently smooth (possessing continuous higher derivatives on [x - 2h, x + 2h]) for Taylor series truncation bounds to hold
assumptions.breaks_when: f lacks the required order of differentiability or exhibits discontinuities within the stencil interval

failure_modes.signature: Severe loss of precision and instability in the derivative estimate as h becomes small
failure_modes.cause: Classical finite-difference approximations are inherently ill-conditioned due to finite-precision cancellation

failure_modes.signature: Higher-order difference approximations fail to converge to the exact derivative
failure_modes.cause: The formal logarithmic operator series h D = \ln(1 + \Delta_h) is not guaranteed to converge even for analytic functions and may be asymptotic

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so finite_difference_jacobian is recorded as a definition
